front: What does a map scale of $1 : 50\,000$ mean?
back: 1 unit on the map represents $50\,000$ of the same units on the ground: 1 cm represents $50\,000$ cm $= 500$ m.
The scale written as a fraction with numerator 1, such as $\frac{1}{50\,000}$. It has no units.

front: How many centimetres are there in 1 km?
How many square metres are there in 1 hectare? How many hectares in $1\ \text{km}^2$?
How do you change a map distance into an actual distance at scale $1 : n$?
back: Multiply by $n$, then convert the units (for example cm to km by dividing by $100\,000$).

front: How do you change an actual distance into a map distance at scale $1 : n$?
back: Convert the distance into the map unit (usually cm), then divide by $n$.

front: At scale $1 : n$, what does $1\ \text{cm}^2$ on the map represent?
back: $n^2\ \text{cm}^2$: the area scale is the square of the length scale.
notes: At $1 : 25\,000$: 1 cm represents 250 m, so $1\ \text{cm}^2$ represents $62\,500\ \text{m}^2$.

front: An 18 km road is 9 cm long on a map. What is the scale?
Which shows more detail: a $1 : 10\,000$ map or a $1 : 250\,000$ map?
back: The $1 : 10\,000$ map (a larger scale): each centimetre covers less ground.

front: Does a scale drawing change the angles of a shape?
back: No. Lengths are scaled; angles stay the same.
